research_scope: Static source and documentation review of agent, harness, provider, tool, MCP, extension, RAG, automation, security, server, database and React interface paths; public primary-source repository/documentation research for all three competitors.
files_inspected_in_depth: 25 Abyx source/config files were read directly for execution-path analysis; the 183-file non-dependency/non-generated project inventory was catalogued and cross-referenced by targeted symbol/route searches. A full line-by-line review of every catalogued file was not completed. Generated artifacts, dependencies and opaque binaries were not treated as source.
files_excluded: Installed app/frontend/node_modules (third-party dependencies), app/dist (generated bundle), .git internals, archive abyx_frontend.zip, binary icon/image/ODT assets and high-volume project logs; directories and presence were catalogued. They are excluded because they do not establish active application source behavior or require specialized extraction/runtime inspection.
tests_not_performed: No UI launched or accessibility/device testing performed
No provider/API calls or model inference
known_limitations: Competitor default branches are mutable; exact audit-date commit SHAs were not independently pinned. Short SHAs are historical snapshot references only.
No runtime execution, dependency audit, threat-model exercise, or hardware performance measurement was performed.
Abyx had a dirty working tree before audit; findings include pre-existing edits and cannot be attributed to the committed HEAD alone.
Several status classifications are static-source confidence, not runtime verification.
research_confidence: High for inspected static call paths and directly visible behavior; medium for broad subsystem coverage; low for runtime reliability/performance and claims that require execution.
